The Matsu Meridian draws this comprehensive 31-obligation set primarily because it is a large container ship (92,400 GT, 8,200 TEU) built in 2019 operating on long-haul international routes (Singapore–Rotterdam) on HFO/VLSFO fuel. This profile triggers obligations across all major maritime regimes: SOLAS and ISPS-A due to size and international service; MARPOL Annexes I, IV, V, and VI due to fuel type, operational areas covering multiple jurisdictions, and built-year proximity to stringent post-2015 NOx and post-2020 sulphur regulations; BWM requirements due to international trading across ballast water regions; MLC as a cargo vessel; and international certificates (Load Line, Tonnage, AFS, Bunkers, Nairobi, IHM). The Asia–Europe trading pattern is especially determinative, as it triggers both Paris MoU and Tokyo MoU PSC regimes and subjects the vessel to EU-MRV carbon reporting. The 2019 build year places it firmly under modern IMO 2030 carbon intensity (CII) and SEEMP Phase III regimes, while HFO/VLSFO fuel carriage mandates the full MARPOL-VI pollution prevention suite including fuel consumption data collection (DCS/CII). No exemptions or reduced requirements apply to this large, modern, internationally-trading container vessel.

6 items accepted, 5 rejected and awaiting resubmission.

Matsu Kestrel draws this comprehensive 33-obligation set primarily as a container ship of 13,760 GT operating in international waters on the Asia-Pacific intra-regional trade lane. The vessel's Post-Panamax size, general cargo container design, and 2008 build year trigger the full suite of SOLAS, MARPOL, and specialized maritime conventions. Matsu Solace is assigned a comprehensive regulatory obligation set driven primarily by its classification as a chemical/products tanker operating internationally under Marshall Islands flag. The 2021 build year places it under current SOLAS, MARPOL, and IMO 2030+ frameworks requiring modern safety, security, pollution prevention, and energy efficiency systems. As a tanker carrying hazardous cargo (noxious liquid substances and oil products), it triggers Annex I, II, and VI MARPOL obligations including oil record books, NLS certificates, and cargo documentation. The vessel's size (29,900 GT) and international trading pattern (Middle East–India) necessitate comprehensive statutory surveys, GMDSS equipment, navigational systems, ballast water management, and ship security protocols. Its dual fuel capability (HFO/VLSFO) and recent construction mandate sulphur compliance, fuel oil data reporting, CII ratings, and SEEMP implementation. Additional requirements for maritime labour certification, load line compliance, tonnage certification, insurance documentation, and hazardous materials inventory complete the profile expected of a modern, internationally-trading tanker.

The 2015 build year triggers modern SOLAS, MARPOL, and ballast water management regimes, while its size (>500 GT) and international trading expose it to the full suite of statutory surveys, GMDSS, navigational system carriage, oil pollution prevention, sewage, garbage management, ballast water control, and crew certification requirements.
